chapter: Earl King, later career and gear
title: Earl King's song and Mitchell's original arrangement
summary: How Earl brought the song, comparison of arrangements, rehearsal at the Blue Eagle.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well how did Earl bring the song to you? What did it sound like when Earl brought it?
Well he just, he sang it to me like the same way he sang it on there. But I put my eye there of how the horns were supposed to go.
So that's all you had heard was what Earl sang to you? He didn't have played on the guitar?
Yeah he'd play it and show me how it'd go and all like that, you know. You know. Yeah. I wish I had that around my mind. I don't know what happened, you know, if I had it, man.
Well how was it different from Waddell?
Well the horns, the bass figure was different, plus the horns was around different. Mine was just as effective as his, but you know you got the head to the hitch, you know.
I remember we rehearsing at the, they're the place called Blue Eagle on Felicity Street. We rehearsing at Big Airman and all of them was there, man.
The whole group was on their session?
No, no, not all of them, but a lot of them, you know. Because see this happened about a year or so before they recorded it, you know.
Earl already had the tune in his head. Yeah.
